Subject: Archive-tiering partner discovery — Orsay & storage options

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for taking the intro last week. Follow-up from our internal product + partnerships sync: we think there could be a tight fit between Orsay's archival tiering capabilities and Redwood's hybrid embeddings storage strategy (hot GPU-backed KV + cold S3/policy-based tiering).

High-level asks for a discovery call:
- Typical retention profiles you see for long-tail embeddings (30/90/365 days).
- How you handle rehydration latency for prefix/KV cache reuse.
- Whether you expose cold-restore APIs we can call from the serving runtime.
- Any existing integrations with Pinecone, pgvector, or object stores (S3/GCS).

Can you share a short architecture sketch (PNG/PDF) and any perf numbers for rehydration at 1k/10k vectors? We can then propose a 4-week pilot matrix (small production traffic + cost/runbook).

Proposed times for a 45-min joint call next week: Tue 10/05 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 10/06 13:00-13:45 PT. Let me know what works and whether you'd like to invite someone from Pinecone (we've CC'd a proposed contact).

Attaching a short list of internal questions to help you prep.

Thanks,
--
Soojin Lee
Head of Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-1224

From: Lina Park <lina.park@orsaydata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@orsaydata.com
Date: 2027-10-03T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Archive-tiering partner discovery — Orsay & storage options

Hi Soojin (and team),

Great to hear — we're excited to explore this. Quick answers inline below and I attached a compact sketch.

- Retention profiles: customers vary; most common patterns are 30/90/365 with a heavy long-tail where ~18% of vectors are accessed <1x/month after 90 days.
- Rehydration latency: cold->warm rehydration for a 1k-vector batch is typically 120-500ms depending on object store egress and whether we parallelize chunk reads. For 10k it's 800ms-2.1s unless you prefetch.
- APIs: yes, we provide a RESTful cold-restore endpoint and a streaming rehydration endpoint that returns vectors in chunks.
- Integrations: we have built connectors for S3 and a community adapter for pgvector; we are running a small compatibility test with Pinecone's fallthrough feature but not GA yet.

I'm attaching our architecture sketch and a short CSV with sample perf numbers. Happy to join the joint call. Tue 10/05 10:00 PT works for our engineering lead.

Best,
Lina Park
Head of Solutions, Orsay Data
lina.park@orsaydata.com

Attachment: tiering-arch-refs.png, orsay-perf-samples.csv

Notes for call prep — internal only:

1) Pilot objective: validate rehydration tail latency and cost per token for two scenarios: (A) Pinecone hot fallback -> Orsay cold restore; (B) pgvector local disk + S3 retrieval via Orsay.
2) Success criteria: 95th percentile rehydration < 1s for 1k batches; incremental cost < 0.2 cents per 1k tokens served (ballpark).
3) Data access/security: need confirmation on KMS/HSM options and whether Orsay keeps metadata/index shims outside customer bucket (we prefer zero-copy S3 reads).
4) Ops/runbook: request they provide an escalation contact and a sample SLA for rehydration during burst windows.

I'll pull the pilot-costs-v1.xlsx and sketch an allocation of 2 dev-weeks + 1 infra-week. Attaching that now.

-Dev
